nodes.body: <<FILL role=setup words=60 beats='Two nights before opening night of the school play The Lantern Keeper, stage manager Cass is doing a final prop check when Ms. Alvarez pulls her aside backstage with terrible timing: lead actor Priya Chandra's family has to move away immediately, and Priya cannot perform.'>>

choices.label: Gather the cast and figure out a plan

nodes.body: <<FILL role=setup words=70 beats='Cass has one rehearsal and one dress rehearsal left before the curtain rises, and three different ways to save the show, each pulling the cast in a different direction.'>>

choices.label: Ask understudy Marcus to step in
Redistribute Priya's lines among the cast
Rework the show into an ensemble format

nodes.body: <<FILL role=explore words=100 beats='Cass finds Marcus Webb, the shy understudy, restocking props backstage and convinces him to take over the lead role of the Lantern Keeper with only two nights to prepare. At blocking rehearsal the next day, Marcus freezes the moment he has to cross center stage under the lights, stage fright taking hold in front of the whole cast.'>>

choices.label: Let Marcus step back from the role
Push forward with Marcus visibly shaken
Spend the last two nights coaching him through it

nodes.body: <<FILL role=ending words=90 beats='Marcus admits he can't do it, and Cass spends the last two nights scrambling to cut the role down to something the crew can read aloud instead.'>>
<<FILL role=ending words=90 beats='Marcus goes on visibly nervous, voice shaking through every scene, but he never stops, and the show limps across the finish line intact.'>>
<<FILL role=transition words=35 beats='Cass spends every spare minute over the next two nights running lines and confidence drills with Marcus in the empty auditorium.'>>

choices.label: Continue

nodes.body: <<FILL role=climax words=100 beats='Opening night has arrived, and Marcus stands alone in the spotlight for the Lantern Keeper's closing monologue, the moment all the coaching was for.'>>

choices.label: Marcus delivers it perfectly
Marcus stumbles but the cast helps him recover
Marcus gets through it imperfectly but real

nodes.body: <<FILL role=ending words=90 beats='Marcus finds his footing and delivers the closing monologue clean and clear, and the auditorium rises into applause as the lantern prop glows steady in his hand.'>>
<<FILL role=ending words=90 beats='Marcus's voice cracks, Jules mouths the next line from the wings, and he catches it and finishes with real fire as the cast erupts into a standing ovation.'>>
<<FILL role=ending words=90 beats='Marcus finishes shaky but honest, and afterward realizes the stumble taught him more about holding a stage than a perfect run ever could.'>>

<<FILL role=explore words=100 beats='Cass gathers Jules Okafor and two other cast members backstage to propose splitting Priya's lines among them instead of finding one new lead. At the next rehearsal, the old blocking built for one lead crumbles as three actors collide trying to share the same stage positions.'>>

choices.label: Abandon the split and cut the role instead
Push forward with the uneven three-way split
Spend the last two nights fixing the blocking

nodes.body: <<FILL role=ending words=90 beats='The three-way split collapses into chaos at rehearsal, and Cass has to scrap it and cut Priya's role down to almost nothing just to get through opening night.'>>
<<FILL role=ending words=90 beats='The three actors muddle through their shared lines unevenly, some scenes stronger than others, and the show finishes whole if a little rough around the edges.'>>
<<FILL role=transition words=35 beats='Cass spends two late nights redrawing the blocking chart from scratch so all three actors have room to move.'>>

choices.label: Continue

nodes.body: <<FILL role=climax words=100 beats='Opening night arrives, and the curtain rises on the redistributed show, three actors now carrying what used to be Priya's single role.'>>

choices.label: It flows seamlessly, better than rehearsed
It's shaky backstage but reads fine out front
Jules quietly takes over the trickiest part

nodes.body: <<FILL role=ending words=90 beats='The three actors trade Priya's old lines like they had always shared the role, and the show lands cleaner than any rehearsal.'>>
<<FILL role=ending words=90 beats='The cast pushes through every near-miss cue without the audience catching a single one, and the show closes to warm, unaware applause.'>>
<<FILL role=ending words=90 beats='Jules quietly absorbs the trickiest exchange herself when the others falter, and afterward admits she has never felt so sure of a role.'>>

<<FILL role=explore words=100 beats='Cass pitches Ms. Alvarez a bigger idea: turn the Lantern Keeper's missing scenes into ensemble narration instead of replacing the lead at all. The cast rehearses the new format under brutal time pressure, and by the second run-through it is clear the risk might not be worth it.'>>

choices.label: Scale it back to something safer
Push forward with the rough new version
Spend the last two nights polishing it properly

nodes.body: <<FILL role=ending words=90 beats='Cass pulls back from the reinvention at the last minute, and the cast scrambles to patch together a simpler, safer version for opening night.'>>
<<FILL role=ending words=90 beats='The reimagined show goes up rough around the edges, some ensemble moments landing and others not quite, and the night ends solid if unspectacular.'>>
<<FILL role=transition words=35 beats='Cass and Deja spend two nights tightening every new ensemble scene, cue by cue, until the format finally clicks.'>>

choices.label: Continue

nodes.body: <<FILL role=climax words=100 beats='The curtain rises on opening night, and the reimagined Lantern Keeper's climax, now carried by the whole ensemble instead of one missing lead, is about to be tested live.'>>

choices.label: The new format wows the audience
Cass owns the risk in the curtain speech
The cast reflects on the gamble together after

nodes.body: <<FILL role=ending words=90 beats='The ensemble climax lands with real power, and the audience leaps to its feet for a show that turned crisis into something new.'>>
<<FILL role=ending words=90 beats='Cass steps out for the curtain speech and tells the audience exactly why the show changed, and the risk becomes the story people remember.'>>
<<FILL role=ending words=90 beats='After curtain, the cast sits in a backstage circle talking through what worked and what didn't, and Cass realizes that conversation is its own kind of success.'>>
